style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#faf5ff;strokeColor=#805ad5;strokeWidth=2;fontColor=#44337a;fontSize=18;fontStyle=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacing=16;" value="INSET: SCALING PATH FROM 200 TO 1,000 FARMS | Technical Constraint & Capacity Headroom Analysis" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="460" width="2720" x="40" y="1500" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="scaling_constraint_quote" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#b794f4;strokeWidth=1.5;fontColor=#553c9e;fontSize=14;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;" value="<b>Case Statement Technical Constraint</b>: "The network and ingestion pattern scales from 200 to 1,000 farms without redesigning the addressing or the ingestion point." (Point 3 &amp; Part A, ASM-032, ASM-036)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="2660" x="70" y="1550" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="scale_panel_1" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#d6bcfa;strokeWidth=1.5;fontColor=#2d3748;fontSize=13;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacing=12;" value="<b>1. Architectural Scalability: Identity, Not IP</b><br/><br/>• <b>Zero Cloud Private IP Consumption</b>: Farms DO NOT receive private cloud IP addresses (ASM-032).<br/>• <b>Public Cellular Bearer</b>: Nodes publish over cellular data (or satellite IP bearer) to the regional public endpoint (AWS IoT Core).<br/>• <b>Authentication by Identity</b>: Devices authenticate via mutual TLS with X.509 certificates and FarmId identities, not IP addresses.<br/>• <b>Linear Expansion</b>: Scaling from 200 to 1,000 farms adds 800 device identities to the existing endpoint.<br/>• <b>Zero Network Topology Changes</b>: ZERO subnet, route table, interface endpoint, or CIDR block changes required.<br/>• <b>Store-and-Forward</b>: Local non-volatile encrypted outbox buffers up to 24 hours of readings when signal is absent.<br/>• <b>Transporters &amp; Drones</b>: Transporter phones and drone uploads over public cellular operate on the same identity principle." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="860" x="70" y="1610" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="scale_panel_2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#d6bcfa;strokeWidth=1.5;fontColor=#2d3748;fontSize=13;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacing=12;" value="<b>2. Ingestion Load Scaling (5x Volume)</b><br/><br/>• <b>Pilot Baseline Load at 200 Farms (Case Statement Part A)</b>:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Cultivation: 200 farms x 6 readings/day = 1,200 readings/day<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Active drying (harvest): 100 farms x 24 readings/day = 2,400 readings/day<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Total pilot daily load: <b>3,600 readings/day (~0.04 readings/sec average)</b><br/><br/>• <b>Expanded Load at 1,000 Farms (ASM-036)</b>:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Cultivation: 1,000 farms x 6 readings/day = 6,000 readings/day<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Active drying (harvest): 500 farms x 24 readings/day = 12,000 readings/day<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* Total expanded load: <b>18,000 readings/day (~0.21 readings/sec average)</b><br/><br/>• <b>Capacity Impact</b>: 0.21 readings/second is trivial for managed AWS IoT Core data plane. Ingestion capacity scales elastically without any network redesign." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="860" x="960" y="1610" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="scale_panel_3" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#d6bcfa;strokeWidth=1.5;fontColor=#2d3748;fontSize=13;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacing=12;" value="<b>3. Pessimistic Address Headroom Analysis (telemetry_ingress)</b><br/><br/>Even under a deliberately pessimistic hypothetical bound where every farm consumed one private VPC IP:<br/><br/>• <b>Usable addresses in telemetry_ingress active AZ slots</b>: 3 x 1,019 = <b>3,057 usable IPs</b><br/>• <b>200 farms consumption</b>: 200 IPs (6.5% of tier capacity) -&gt; <b>2,857 free IPs</b><br/>• <b>1,000 farms consumption</b>: 1,000 IPs (32.7% of tier capacity) -&gt; <b>2,057 free IPs</b><br/>• <b>Worst-case single AZ concentration</b>: 1,000 farms fits within ONE single /22 slot (1,019 usable IPs)!<br/>• <b>Additional tier headroom without readdressing</b>:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* az4 slot reserved: 1,019 additional IPs<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;* 8 reserved tier blocks (10.E.112.0/17): 32,768 IPs per environment<br/>• <b>Collection Centers</b>: 10.40.0.0/13 summary route already encompasses fourth department (10.44.0.0/16)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="880" x="1850" y="1610" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="footer_traceability" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=13;fontColor=#4a5568;" value="<b>Traceability &amp; Badges</b>: D04 = Pattern VPC and Tiers (B04 / #24) | D05 = Collection Center Pattern &amp; Association (B05 / #25) | ADR-001 (cloud choice) | ASM-030 to ASM-036 (addressing assumptions) | ASM-080 to ASM-089 (LAN pattern) | PD-009 (closed non-overlapping CIDRs) | PD-050 (Terraform vars) | PD-052 (firewall policies)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="2720" x="40" y="1980" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

NON-OVERLAP VERIFICATION (PROVED)
• Centers vs AWS Supernet: 10.47.255.255 < 10.80.0.0 [PASS]
• AWS Supernet vs Azure: 10.87.255.255 < 10.88.0.0 [PASS]
• AWS Environments: 10.80.255.255 < 10.81.0.0 < 10.82.0.0 [PASS]
• Prefix Boundary Alignment:
* /13 on mod-8 octet (40, 80, 88)
* /14 on mod-4 octet (84)
* /22 on mod-4 octet (all tier subnets: 0, 4, 8, 12, ...)
* /28 on mod-16 octet (transit subnets: 0, 16, 32, 48)
Verified with Python ipaddress module and exact prefix boundaries.

div.div:
Primary WAN & Tunnel Link
• 100 Mbps symmetric internet service (90 Mbps usable payload + 10 Mbps IPsec encapsulation & keepalives)
• Cellular backup link with automatic failover (ASM-088)
• Dual IPsec VPN tunnels from Center Firewall (10.4x.20.1) to AWS Transit Gateway Hub
• Staff Wi-Fi admission (RADIUS / EAP-TLS) validates locally against cached CRL when WAN is down

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 188, 250), rgb(80, 58, 111));

div.div:
Hub Routing & Inter-Zone Policy Enforcement
• TGW Hub terminates center VPN tunnels and attaches to each VPC transit tier (/28)
• Route 10.40.0.0/13 covers present (Cauca, Huila, Tolima) and future departments (10.44.0.0/16, ASM-030)
• Allowed paths through tunnel:
* Logística (10.4x.3.0/24) to VPC application tier (sacks & trips API)
* Ground Station (10.4x.2.10/32) to VPC application and object_storage (S3 interface endpoint)
* Cloud administration tier to Servidores locales (10.4x.10.0/24) for device management
• Strictly denied: telemetry_ingress (bypassed), drone_object_ingress (reserved)

div.div: INSET: SCALING PATH FROM 200 TO 1,000 FARMS | Technical Constraint & Capacity Headroom Analysis

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #553c9e;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#553c9e, #baa4f9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Case Statement Technical Constraint: "The network and ingestion pattern scales from 200 to 1,000 farms without redesigning the addressing or the ingestion point." (Point 3 & Part A, ASM-032, ASM-036)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 188, 250), rgb(80, 58, 111));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 838px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1607px; margin-left: 53px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #2d3748;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#2d3748, #b7bfce); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1. Architectural Scalability: Identity, Not IP
• Zero Cloud Private IP Consumption: Farms DO NOT receive private cloud IP addresses (ASM-032).
• Public Cellular Bearer: Nodes publish over cellular data (or satellite IP bearer) to the regional public endpoint (AWS IoT Core).
• Authentication by Identity: Devices authenticate via mutual TLS with X.509 certificates and FarmId identities, not IP addresses.
• Linear Expansion: Scaling from 200 to 1,000 farms adds 800 device identities to the existing endpoint.
• Zero Network Topology Changes: ZERO subnet, route table, interface endpoint, or CIDR block changes required.
• Store-and-Forward: Local non-volatile encrypted outbox buffers up to 24 hours of readings when signal is absent.
• Transporters & Drones: Transporter phones and drone uploads over public cellular operate on the same identity principle.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 188, 250), rgb(80, 58, 111));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 838px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1607px; margin-left: 943px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #2d3748;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#2d3748, #b7bfce); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
2. Ingestion Load Scaling (5x Volume)
• Pilot Baseline Load at 200 Farms (Case Statement Part A):
* Cultivation: 200 farms x 6 readings/day = 1,200 readings/day
* Active drying (harvest): 100 farms x 24 readings/day = 2,400 readings/day
* Total pilot daily load: 3,600 readings/day (~0.04 readings/sec average)
• Expanded Load at 1,000 Farms (ASM-036):
* Cultivation: 1,000 farms x 6 readings/day = 6,000 readings/day
* Active drying (harvest): 500 farms x 24 readings/day = 12,000 readings/day
* Total expanded load: 18,000 readings/day (~0.21 readings/sec average)
• Capacity Impact: 0.21 readings/second is trivial for managed AWS IoT Core data plane. Ingestion capacity scales elastically without any network redesign.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 188, 250), rgb(80, 58, 111));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 858px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1607px; margin-left: 1833px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #2d3748;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#2d3748, #b7bfce); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
3. Pessimistic Address Headroom Analysis (telemetry_ingress)
Even under a deliberately pessimistic hypothetical bound where every farm consumed one private VPC IP:
• Usable addresses in telemetry_ingress active AZ slots: 3 x 1,019 = 3,057 usable IPs
• 200 farms consumption: 200 IPs (6.5% of tier capacity) -> 2,857 free IPs
• 1,000 farms consumption: 1,000 IPs (32.7% of tier capacity) -> 2,057 free IPs
• Worst-case single AZ concentration: 1,000 farms fits within ONE single /22 slot (1,019 usable IPs)!
• Additional tier headroom without readdressing:
* az4 slot reserved: 1,019 additional IPs
* 8 reserved tier blocks (10.E.112.0/17): 32,768 IPs per environment
• Collection Centers: 10.40.0.0/13 summary route already encompasses fourth department (10.44.0.0/16)
